wurraluh: The Australian white-quilled honey eater (Entomyza albipennis).
wurbagool: A fruit bat (Pteropus medius) native of India. It is similar to the flying fox, but smaller.
wungout: Having the sails set in the manner called wing-and-wing. [Sailors' slang]
wulfenite: Native lead molybdate occurring in tetragonal crystals, usually tabular, and of a bright orange-yellow to red, gray, or brown color; -- also called yellow lead ore.
wull: See 2d Will. Pour out to all that wull. Spenser.
